record.what_it_does: FX audit API scoring bank/card FX rates against live mid-market rates, with MCP server.
record.auth_notes: A static API key (prefix ipx_live_) is sent as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. Keys are generated in the iPayX dashboard under API keys. There is no OAuth, so each end user must supply their own key. The MCP page also mentions an ipx_test_ key format, but the API reference lists only ipx_live_.
record.access_notes: The homepage says API access needs the Credit Pack ($99 one-time for 100 audits) or Unlimited ($299/mo). The Free plan gives 3 lifetime audits. The pricing page does not list API access under any plan, and the API docs only link "Get an API key" to pricing. The MCP docs say free keys get 10 audits/day and 60 rate calls/min, which suggests a free key may exist for the MCP's free tools. That conflicts with the homepage statement.
record.api_breadth_notes: 3 endpoints: audit (single transaction), rates (live mid-market), audit/document (batch document audit). There are also signed audit.completed webhooks. The MCP server has 3 tools: audit_fx_transaction, full_forensic_fx_report (paid), and check_fx_mid_market_rate.
record.mcp_notes: https://hvujzsdwcoweirroubeh.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp-server. The transport appears to be Streamable HTTP (the example sends Accept: application/json, text/event-stream). Auth is Bearer with an ipx_ key. Documented at ipayx.ai/docs/mcp-server.
record.blocker_notes: The API has only 3 endpoints and the product is niche. According to the homepage, API access needs a paid plan (Credit Pack $99 or Unlimited $299/mo). Auth is a per-user API key with no OAuth. A test-key format (ipx_test_) appears only on the MCP docs page, and there is no documented sandbox environment.

evidence.quote: Our deterministic engine scores every FX transaction against the live mid-market rate
Every request requires a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header. Keys start with `ipx_live_`.
Upgrade to the 100-audit Credit Pack or Unlimited for API access, white-label embedding, and forensic PDF exports.
Subscribe to `audit.completed` events to power Zapier triggers, n8n workflows, or your own Slack alerts.

record.needs_human: The page text was read through WebFetch summaries. The quotes match on re-fetch, but the site appears to render client-side, which is likely why the automated verifier failed to match them. Two things still need a human: (1) whether a Free-plan account can create an API key (the homepage and the MCP docs conflict); (2) whether ipx_test_ keys and a test mode actually exist.

changes.why: No WebSocket API is documented. The MCP transport is HTTP with an event-stream Accept header, not WebSocket.
The API reference does not mention test or sandbox keys. Only the MCP page names an ipx_test_ format, with no documented test environment.

changes.new: ...mcp-server, Streamable HTTP (Accept: application/json, text/event-stream), Bearer ipx_ key
changes.why: The docs do not say SSE. The example request uses the Streamable HTTP Accept header.
